item.title: 3 Observations from Indiana men’s basketball’s 90-76 win over Kentucky
item.description: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - NOVEMBER 20: Markus Burton #5 of the Indiana Hoosiers celebrates in the second half of the 90-76 win over the Kentucky Wildcats at Lucas Oil Stadium on November 20, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images Darian DeVries avenged his loss to Kentucky last season with a 14-point win in the rivalry series’ ‘semi-neutral’ game at Lucas Oil Stadium. Indiana remains perfect on the season while the Wildcats fall to 4-2 with lopsided losses to both high major programs they’ve seen this year. Indiana built an early lead in the game before Milan Momcilovic single-handedly brought Kentucky back from the dead. His 22-point first half was enough to kill Indiana’s momentum and give Kentucky a two point lead heading into halftime. DeVries knew that the key to the second half would be slowing him down and his group came out and did just that. Momcilovic didn’t make a three in the entire second half and Indiana finally built the lead that eluded them early in the game, eventually winning 90-76. Here are three observations from the game: Bryce Lindsay It’s not often that your most important player is a bench guy, but Bryce Lindsay is looking like the best sixth-man in the country and has been a huge difference-maker for Indiana’s perfect start. It starts with his willingness to come off the bench. Lindsay started all 31 games at Villanova last season and clearly has the ability to be a high-major starter. Whatever the conversation was to get him to accept this role at Indiana, the fit is a testament to both he and DeVries. Part of what has made this work so well is that he tends to share the floor with one of Darren Harris or Markus Burton, allowing him to alternate between shooter and driver. The other part of it is simply his ability to hit shots at all levels, often with more than one defender on him. His 3-point shooting will always be what jumps off the page, especially with the range he showed against Arkansas, but tonight showed his versatility inside. Kentucky knew it struggled to defend the perimeter, so he punished their overly aggressive close-outs with drives or by drawing fouls from beyond the arc. He’s going to miss some frustrating ones with the green light he has, but Lindsay has shown a willingness and ability to hit the hardest shots all over the floor. This is an invaluable piece to have coming off the bench. Versatility I’ve been waiting for this team to establish either an interior or perimeter offensive identity this season, but it turns out Indiana’s real strength might be its ability to do both. DeVries knew that he had the size and experience over Arkansas inside and fed Samet Yigitoglu and Aiden Sherrell inside accordingly. Malachi Moreno negated that advantage against Kentucky, so DeVries fell back on the guard play that helped him beat Syracuse. What I like most about this is that the team has maintained some balance in both styles. DeVries left Yigitoglu on the floor even

item.title: The Prediction: Indiana Hoosiers
item.description: BLOOMINGTON, INDIANA - OCTOBER 26: Keleki Latu #85 of the Washington Huskies makes a catch against the Indiana Hoosiers at Memorial Stadium on October 26, 2024 in Bloomington, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images Tomorrow afternoon, the Huskies will welcome the defending national champ, Indiana, to Montlake as they search for an upset against the number 9 team in the land. Our staff has their picks below! Andrew Berg (5-4 SU, 4-5 ATS) The Huskies return home after a successful road trip in a week where 7/9 Big 10 home teams are underdogs. Of course, the Dawgs have not lit the world on fire at home this year, losing to Minnesota, Iowa, and Penn St at Husky Stadium (naming rights deal be damned, I will continue to say Husky Stadium). Indiana is the defending National Champions but has not looked as dominant as they did a year ago. In fact, they changed QBs to Grant Wilson last week against USC and the 6th year Old Dominion transfer looked rock solid. In fact, that game was a bounce-back of sorts for Indiana, who struggled to beat Michigan and Minnesota in the two previous games. Regardless of who plays QB, the RB duo of Beebe and Richard has kept the offense moving all season. The Husky defense has forced opponents to drive the length of the field and avoid making mistakes. It has worked for most of the season and led to lots of forced turnovers. Indiana has been disciplined and physical enough to avoid those mistakes, so it could be a tough game for the defense to make big plays. And that’s the side of the ball where the Huskies have more often had the advantage this year. The Husky offense had a strong first half against Michigan St last week, albeit only to the tune of 14 points on the board. Demond Williams finally looked like the QB from 2025 who trusted his arm to make difficult throws to talented receivers. Chris Lawson was primarily responsible for another win and has emerged as the standout skill-position player on the team. All the same, Indiana’s defense has been rock solid all year. They stymie teams who run the ball much better than the Huskies, so it is likely to be another one-dimensional attack. I don’t think UW will be anywhere close to being shut out at home, but I don’t think they can score enough to keep this one within reach. Indiana 30 – Washington 17 Luke Kemper (1-0 SU, 0-1 ATS) Unfortunately I think this is going to be a lopsided game and feel like the first half of the Iowa and Penn State games. The only difference is that Indiana will get it done through the air instead of on the ground. Charlie Becker and Nick Marsh are easily the best receiving duo that UW will have faced all year. After giving up chunk plays last week to Michigan State, one of the worst offenses in the country in that category, it is a big concern going into the game. Karnley and Robinson will need to play great, but McLaughlin and RDA need to play even better to give help in pass defense and stopping RB Lee Beebe Jr. UW’s

item.title: No. 15 Vanderbilt Handles Business to Stay Undefeated
item.description: Photo by: ANDREW NELLES Vanderbilt continued its impressive start to the 2026-27 basketball season Friday night, defeating UCF 82-74 at Memorial Gymnasium in Nashville. The Commodores used a strong first half performance and timely scoring down the stretch to take care of a difficult opponent and improve to 6-0. Coming into the matchup, Vanderbilt was ranked No. 15 nationally and had looked dominant through its first five games. UCF presented a tougher challenge, entering Nashville with a 4-1 record and one of the nation’s most productive scorers in Dior Johnson. The Knights were hoping to earn a major road victory, but Vanderbilt quickly showed why it has become one of the teams to watch early in the season. Vanderbilt Builds an Early Advantage The Commodores came out with plenty of energy, taking control of the opening half with an efficient offensive performance. Vanderbilt found ways to attack the basket, move the ball and create scoring opportunities while making life difficult for UCF on the other end. Tyler Tanner played an important role in the early success, providing scoring and helping Vanderbilt establish control. His ability to contribute offensively and create opportunities for teammates gave the Commodores an important advantage. UCF struggled to find its shooting rhythm. The Knights had difficulty getting consistent production from the field, allowing Vanderbilt to build separation on the scoreboard. The Commodores carried a 38-29 advantage into halftime, putting themselves in a strong position heading into the final 20 minutes. Knights Make a Push, but Vanderbilt Responds UCF came out looking to make things interesting in the second half. The Knights increased their offensive production, scoring 45 points after halftime compared to 29 in the opening period. Dior Johnson continued to be an important part of the UCF offense, but the Knights needed more consistent contributions from the rest of the lineup to complete the comeback. Vanderbilt also remained productive offensively, adding 44 second-half points to keep UCF from getting within striking distance. Whenever the Knights looked capable of building momentum, the Commodores found ways to answer. That ability to respond ultimately made the difference. Vanderbilt did not allow UCF’s improved second-half offense to erase the advantage it had created before the break. Commodores Improve to 6-0 The final buzzer confirmed an 82-74 Vanderbilt victory. The eight-point win moves the Commodores to 6-0, while UCF falls to 4-2. The result gives Vanderbilt another important victory against a power-conference opponent and continues its strong opening stretch. The Commodores have demonstrated that they can win comfortably, but Friday’s contest also showed they can handle a more competitive game when an opponent makes a second-half push. item.title: MVP, box score, and Twitter reactions to Kentucky Wildcats’ loss to Indiana
item.description: Heading into halftime, Kentucky Basketball had as much momentum as they have had at any point in any game all season. The Wildcats closed the half on a 12-0 run to lead Indiana 47-45 at halftime inside Lucas Oil Stadium. Milan Momcilovic was making it rain, and Kentucky’s defense was getting stops. Then, the script completely flipped in the second half. Kentucky’s defense couldn’t stop fouling, and the Wildcats’ offense couldn’t stop turning the ball over. It led to a frustrating second half where Indiana gradually and frustratingly pulled away for a 90-76 win. The curse in Indianapolis continues for the Cats. Kentucky is now 4-2 on the season and 0-2 against Power Four teams. Next up for the Cats: A home game next Friday night against Wichita State. MVP: Milan Momcilovic Easy. Momcilovic exploded for 22 points and five three-pointers in the first half. He finished with a game-high 28 points. He can shoot, clearly. Now we just need to see it in a Kentucky uniform for 40 minutes in a Power Four game. Box Score First Half It was an offensive explosion on both sides early. The first media timeout didn’t come until 12:50 left in the first half. By that point, it was 19-19. Both teams were 8-14 from the floor, with a combined 5-8 from three-point range. Kentucky had five assists to no turnovers in the first 7:10 of the game, and Milan Momcilovic had seven points and two three-pointers. From there, though, Indiana kept up their shot-making, hitting six-of-eight to stretch out an 11-point lead to 36-25. Part of that stretch included an 8-0 run over 52 seconds that saw three-pointers from the Hoosiers’ Bryce Lindsay and Markus Burton. Alex Wilkins responded with five points to give the Cats a 38-30 lead with 7:25 left in the first half. Kentucky was keeping it close, but where Indiana stayed in front was on offensive rebounding. Then again, it helps to have Milan Momcilovic. The best shooter in the country exploded late in the first half, sparking a 10-0 run with back-to-back three-pointers that tied the game 45-45 with 1:25 remaining. Momcilovic was explosive in the first half, scoring 22 points and hitting five-of-six three-pointers. He was 8-10 from the floor overall, and he also dished out two assists. Zoom Diallo hit a short jumper with seven seconds remaining to give Kentucky a 47-45 lead at halftime. With 10 points, Diallo was Kentucky’s other double-digit scorer in the first half. Kentucky finished the first half 20-35 from the field and 6-10 from three-point range. They had eight assists to just two turnovers. Indiana shot 44.4 percent from the floor but missed 10 of their last 11 shots. They also went the final 3:40 of the first half without scoring. The Hoosiers were 8-18 from three-point range. While they won the rebound battle 18-14, they had three turnovers to their eight assists. Second Half Indiana came out firing in the second half, with Aiden Sherrell making back-to-back three-pointers to put the Hoosiers back up by two possessions at 5

item.title: 49ers’ Kyle Shanahan drops ‘awesome’ reaction to viral Mac Jones video
item.description: Credit: Cary Edmondson-Imagn Images 49ers’ Kyle Shanahan drops ‘awesome’ reaction to viral Mac Jones video appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Kyle Shanahan has an all-time great coaching battle against Brian Flores coming up in Week 11 with the 49ers set to host the Vikings in Mexico City. The NFC playoff picture looks clear now with the 49ers in the driver’s seat, trailed closely by Minnesota, Detroit and Chicago in the NFC North and the Seahawks further down in the West. Ahead of Week 11’s Mexico City clash, Kyle Shanahan took a break from serious stuff to discuss Mac Jones ’ viral boombox walkout video. Mac Jones went viral this week for his 49ers boombox walkout vibe, but it's not the first time he's made waves. Jones went to the front last season w/ ex-Pats teammate Kendrick Bourne. Now Deebo is back. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) In January: "I wanted to be at the front, and they wanted me to be there." pic.twitter.com/XBX7EFgvv7 — David Lombardi (@LombardiHimself) November 20, 2026 He said he liked the video according to 49ers blogger Coach Yac on X. “Yeah I saw that. My kids sent it to me. It was awesome, but that’s how we see Mac every day. If you just saw it once, you’d be like, ‘Who’s this corny white dude?’ But you don’t see it at all because he is like that all the time. He is always upbeat. He is always having fun.” The 49ers’ backup QB has appeared in two games this season but hasn’t recorded a stat. He is one of the NFL’s unquestioned top backup quarterbacks after a 2,000-plus yard, 13-touchdown season with the 49ers in 11 games in 2025 and is a former first round pick. Jones got a positive comment from Trent Williams on his off-field impact recently. The 49ers are a true team in every sense of the word, and Jones’ presence is a big reason why. item.title: 'They should be willing to flip-flop': Mike Florio suggests Thanksgiving flex games
item.description: Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images, NBC Sports Next week’s slate of NFL games on Thanksgiving has a lot to like about it. In keeping with tradition, the Detroit Lions and Dallas Cowboys will both host a game on Turkey Day, while the third, rotating primetime game will be hosted by the Buffalo Bills. But it’s possible that one aspect of the traditional Thanksgiving Day schedule is due for a change. The Lions are always the early game on Thanksgiving, while the Cowboys kickoff around 4:30 p.m. ET. The simplest reason behind this fact is time zones, but because of the relative state of both teams and the importance of their upcoming games next Thursday, Mike Florio believes the time may be right for the NFL to embrace flexing its schedule on the holiday. This year, the Lions host the Chicago Bears in a game that will have huge ramifications in the NFC North, the best division in football by a healthy margin so far this season. The Cowboys, whose defense can’t do anything, are hosting the Philadelphia Eagles, who can’t do anything on either side of the ball. While that NFC East matchup was an easy sell on paper before the start of the season, it sure looks a lot less appealing now than it did in Week 1. Florio has high expectations for the Lions-Bears game, even if it is going to start early. “I think the ratings for that game are going to be through the roof. I’m starting to think it might even be larger than the 47.7 million from last year,” Florio said, referencing the massive rating the Lions brought in with their Thanksgiving game against the Packers in 2025. “People are going to appreciate the fact that the good game is the early game. The middle game, Eagles-Cowboys, who cares? If you want to see a good, compelling, dramatic football game, that’s the one. It used to be the other way around. How many years was the Lions game just, ‘That’s what’s on TV — somebody is rolling into Detroit to beat up the Lions, it’s going to be 23–6 in the fourth quarter, let’s just get this thing over with and let’s bring out the Cowboys’? The vibe has completely shifted.” Florio argued that given the league’s broad flex privileges when it comes to its primetime schedule, a similar ability should be established to allow the league to move the better Thanksgiving game into the afternoon slot. “Frankly, they flex everything else. They should be willing to flip-flop the Lions and Cowboys games. They should be willing to say, ‘Alright we’re starting the Cowboys game at basically 12:30 p.m. ET, and we’re going to delay the Lions game.’ You give people a week, two weeks notice. We would’ve known a week or two ago that Bears-Lions is the far more compelling game. If you want to blow out the number at 4:30 p.m. ET, you put Bears-Lions in that window.” The ratings for Bears-Lions on Thanksgiving will be through the roof. They’d be even bigger if the kickoff times for Bears-Lions and Eagles-Cowboys were flipped. https://t.co/LNn9rliQBn — PFT Live (@PFT_Live) November 19, 2026 W

item.title: Sandpapergate peace deal: AUS players' union chief urges shared responsibility, slams 'unacceptable' hounding of Pat Cummins
item.description: Sandpapergate peace deal: AUS players' union chief urges shared responsibility, slams 'unacceptable' hounding of Pat Cummins originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Australian Players’ Union boss Paul Marsh wants everyone linked to the 2018 tour to share blame. He also says the intrusion into Pat Cummins’ private life has gone too far. Marsh believes a shared acknowledgement could help the sport heal and move on. Paul Marsh calls on Pat Cummins and Cricket Australia to take collective responsibility to end Sandpapergate crisis A peace deal of sorts for the Sandpapergate saga is what Paul Marsh, the chief executive of the Australian Cricketers’ Association (ACA), is now proposing. He wants every member of the 2018 touring group in South Africa, Pat Cummins and the other fast bowlers included, to stand alongside Cricket Australia (CA) and accept collective responsibility for what happened. He has stayed in regular contact with Cummins, Usman Khawaja and other players and support staff from that period, former coach Darren Lehmann among them. Out of those conversations, Marsh has concluded that an admission of shared accountability offers the group its best chance of moving forward, even if some of those on the tour continue to deny any specific knowledge of sandpaper. The proposal arrives at a delicate moment, since the dispute over who knew what, and when, has split opinion inside the game and raised awkward questions about the Australian captain himself. The current tension traces back to 2021, when Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon put their names to a joint statement, where they insisted that they had no prior knowledge of sandpaper being “taken onto the field”. Cummins has since doubled down on his position, and he now says he had no knowledge of any ball tampering, either before the tour or during it. Those claims have now been challenged by Khawaja, David Warner, Chadd Sayers and Cameron Bancroft, and their accounts have fed a growing credibility problem for Australian cricket. The situation is made more sensitive by the ACA’s own makeup, because Khawaja is a current director of the body that Marsh leads. Cummins is a former director, and so is his manager, Neil Maxwell. More to follow...

item.title: Do women control their husbands?
item.description: By Chioma Gabriel, Editor, Special Features It is often said that women are a necessary evil, a desirable calamity and a domestic peril. It all depends on where one is standing. In traditional African societies, a woman’s place was said to be in the kitchen, from where she was expected to work her way into her husband’s heart through his stomach. Women were traditionally expected to be seen but not heard. They were like shadows trailing their husbands, with little or no opportunity to express opinions on matters affecting the family and society. They were often regarded as acquired possessions whose primary responsibilities were to bear children and provide labour on the farms. They had little or no say in the scheme of things. A similar pattern appears in some biblical accounts, where headcounts excluded women and children. When Jesus fed the 5,000 and the 4,000, the recorded figures referred to the men, with women and children excluded from the count. In the early Christian community, Paul’s instruction required women to remain silent in church and ask their husbands questions at home. Although interpretations of this passage differ among Christian scholars, it has historically been cited to support restrictions on women’s public religious participation. Despite these historical and cultural limitations, women have, in different ways, exercised considerable influence over men, including their husbands. Biblical accounts The Bible contains several accounts of women whose actions, decisions or influence significantly shaped the lives of men. Eve persuaded Adam to eat the forbidden fruit after the serpent tempted her in the Garden of Eden. Jezebel manipulated her husband, King Ahab, and orchestrated the murder of Naboth to acquire his vineyard. Delilah used persistent pressure and deception to make Samson reveal the secret of his extraordinary strength. Sapphira conspired with her husband, Ananias, to deceive the apostles about the proceeds from the sale of their property. Michal helped David escape from King Saul but later confronted and despised him over his public dancing before God. Bathsheba, working alongside the prophet Nathan, intervened to ensure that David fulfilled his promise that Solomon would succeed him as king. Sarah persuaded Abraham to have a child through her maidservant, Hagar, and later demanded that Hagar and Ishmael be sent away. Rebekah orchestrated a family deception by persuading her son Jacob to disguise himself as Esau and obtain Isaac’s blessing. Herodias influenced her daughter to demand the head of John the Baptist from her husband, Herod Antipas. Job’s wife, overwhelmed by their suffering, urged her husband to curse God and die. Mary and Martha also demonstrated the emotional influence women could have. When their brother, Lazarus, died, their grief deeply moved Jesus, who wept before raising him from the dead. item.title: Nets shake up everything but the outcome in heartbreaking fourth straight loss
item.description: Nets magic Team meetings. Lineup changes. Whatever it took. Brooklyn tried everything to shake up a three-game losing skid. The Nets finally showed some heart Friday night. But then they got it broken in a 113-111 loss to the Magic in front of a crowd of 17,067 at Barclays Center. Franz Wagner hit a go-ahead 14-footer with 2.8 seconds left, and Julius Randle missed a desperation 3-pointer at the buzzer on the other end. Brooklyn Nets forward Danny Wolf shoots as Orlando Magic center Wendell Carter Jr. defends on Friday, Nov. 20, 2026, at Barclays Center in Brooklyn, N.Y. Robert Sabo for NY Post Randle finished with a team-high 27 points, and Brooklyn fought. They just couldn’t quite close. After the Nets (3-12) embarrassed themselves in Wednesday’s 137-107 non-effort against Chicago , they held a team meeting, with some real talk about what went wrong and how to fix it. Friday’s effort showed it wasn’t all just talk. It just wasn’t quite enough. “No one wants to lose like we did [Wednesday] … so a lot needed to be said. A lot of guys have been doing a lot of talking; we’ve all been doing a lot of talking,” Michael Porter Jr. said. “We’ve gotta string some games together. We’ve had spurts of good responses after really bad games, but that has to be a consistent theme. We can’t just let that be responses to really bad losses.” Wednesday qualified as a really bad loss, the worst of a disappointing season. Brooklyn Nets forward Julius Randle (30) goes up for a shot against the Orlando Magic at Barclays Center in Brooklyn, N.Y., Friday, Nov. 20, 2026. Robert Sabo for NY Post After that, the Nets had a look-in-the-mirror meeting that sources said included not only players, but also coaches. “Everybody collectively. It was a good conversation, and everybody pitched into what they saw,” Porter said. “There was a lot of internal discussion that I’ll keep between the team. But just realizing we got to be better and addressing what needed to be addressed.” One thing that coach Jordi Fernández did was shuffle his rotations. Orlando Magic forward Franz Wagner dunks during the second quarter against the Brooklyn Nets on Friday, Nov. 20, 2026, at Barclays Center in Brooklyn, N.Y. Robert Sabo for NY Post Egor Dëmin — last year’s lottery pick — was pulled out of the starting lineup. He was brought off the bench for the first time since Nov. 5, 2025, his rookie season. Instead, Fernández went with 6-foot-11 forward Danny Wolf as a jumbo shooting guard . And the move paid immediate dividends. Wolf poured in 20 points and five rebounds, finishing a team-high plus-15. Rookie Mikel Brown Jr. added a career-high-tying 18 points. Porter, who admitted not having the right energy in his five-point, 1-of-7 effort Wednesday, bounced back well. His layup off a Day’Ron Sharpe feed gave the Nets a 63-62 edge coming out of the half. The Nets coughed up 10 unanswered Orlando points, the run capped by Wagner (game-high 35 points). item.title: F1 qualifying results: Las Vegas Grand Prix
item.description: (Photo by Guido De Bortoli/LAT Images) George Russell led the way in the third and final hour of practice at the Las Vegas Grand Prix Friday evening. But will the Mercedes driver top the timing sheets during the all-important qualifying hour later tonight? Russell led teammate Kimi Antonelli and McLaren’s Lando Norris in FP3 Friday evening, with the veteran Mercedes driver posting a lap of 1:34.041, almost a full second ahead of Antonelli, who was 0.911 seconds off the pace. Charles Leclerc and Franco Colapinto rounded out the top five. Friday’s FP3 session was the only representative session of the weekend so far, as both FP1 and FP2 on Thursday were compromised by wet weather. The biggest story so far in Las Vegas might just be the list of drivers taking a grid penalty due to new components. Five drivers — Antonelli, Lance Stroll, Oliver Bearman, Oscar Piastri, and Carlos Sainz — have already taken on new components ahead of the Las Vegas Grand Prix and are facing grid drops at the start of the race. Antonelli is facing a five-place grid drop, while Stroll, Piastri, and Sainz are facing ten-place grid drops. Bearman, who is taking on a fifth Internal Combustion Engine, turbocharger, exhaust, and MGU-K, and as those components all exceed the permitted amount per season, he will start at the back of the grid. But who will take pole position? We will find out soon enough. Qualifying for the Las Vegas Grand Prix gets rolling at 11:00 p.m. Eastern Time on Friday night, so check back early and often for updates! And as always, download the new SB Nation app , join the F1 Community, and follow the qualifying thread live! item.title: Michael Strahan Names Giants Legend the True MVP of Super Bowl XLII Over Eli Manning Ahead of Netflix’s ‘Untold’ Documentary
item.description: Fox Sports Media Day, New Orleans, Louisiana, USA Former Football player and TV host Michael Strahan During the Fox Sports Media Day at the New Orleans Convention Center in New Orleans, Louisiana, USA Copyright: xMartyxJean-Louisx ©IMAGO/Marty Jean Louis Former New York Giants defensive end Justin Tuck had a picture-perfect career in the NFL. He played nine seasons with the New York Giants, where he won two Super Bowl rings, made two Pro Bowls, and was named first-team All-Pro. Yet for his teammate, former New York Giants defensive end Michael Strahan, Tuck missed one accolade that left his resume short of being perfect. To Strahan, Tuck deserved that honor, which was handed to quarterback Eli Manning. “One thing I will say, and I love him. We had him on the podcast. I love my guy Eli Manning. But this right here is the MVP of Super Bowl 42. I love Eli,” Strahan shared on the Hustle Like You’re Broke podcast. “Made some great plays. They did. They shot the second one, but the first one was right here because I’m rushing and I’m thinking I’m doing good. I’m like, I’m quick. I’m like, how the hell did they get there already? So, [laughter] he, but he had the diversity that I didn’t have to play inside and outside. “And I think that’s the one thing that he may not give himself enough credit for is it’s two totally different positions. So, to be able to switch your mind and have a body that you can do those things in is amazing. But also when you’re the guy and you got two or three guys every play hitting you, it completely changed the way football looks to you.” In Super Bowl XLII, New York’s Super Bowl hopes appeared to be hanging by a thread when Manning launched a desperate pass on third-and-5 near midfield with the Giants trailing by four. It was the kind of throw that could easily have resulted in an interception and ended the game. David Tyree somehow came up with it, trapping the ball against his helmet. The spectacular effort kept the Giants’ championship hopes alive. Strahan's surprising MVP take on the Giants' greatest moment challenges everything you thought you knew about that legendary Super Bowl run. Subscribe for the untold stories reshaping NFL history. That catch gave Manning another opportunity to lead his team downfield, and the quarterback made it count. He delivered a touchdown pass to Plaxico Burress. However, Strahan believes that Tuck also stood out by having two sacks in the Super Bowl XLII. Yet the award went to Manning. After all, Tuck also created another opportunity by forcing a Brady fumble that Osi Umenyiora recovered. The story repeated in Super Bowl XLVI. New England’s offense had been one of the most productive units in the NFL throughout the 2011 season, averaging 32.1 points per game. However, the Patriots managed just 17 against the Giants, with Tuck playing a major role in keeping Brady and company under pressure. His two sacks, three tackles, and three quarterback hits might not fully capture the impact he had

item.title: Four takeaways from Virginia’s 103-61 win against Loyola MD
item.description: The undefeated Virginia Cavaliers (7-0) secured a 42-point win over the Loyola Maryland Greyhounds (1-5) on Friday night. The 103-61 victory was not unexpected, but these non-conference games give an early look into the team’s potential for the season. Based on Friday’s 100-point game, Virginia’s crystal ball is looking pretty bright. Here are my four takeaways from the statement win. The ’Hoos have a leader in Sam Lewis With 20 points in only 24 minutes, it’s fair to say Sam Lewis didn’t waste a second on the floor. He executed along the three-point line, had a few drives to the basket, and in the first half, had a steal that led to his fast-break dunk. He tallied four rebounds, four assists, and 2 steals and went 3-of-5 from deep. He’s playing a 360-degree game, orchestrating the offense, containing his man on D, and playing a critical role in the team’s energy. He and Chance Mallory make up one of Virginia’s most dangerous pairings. Mallory’s 10 points and six assists were the perfect complement. With the two of them regularly on the floor together, the offense is anything but stale. Loyola shot well, but it was no competition for No. 4 Virginia If you look at the score, the ’Hoos dominated. And while the game itself didn’t feel like much of a competition for Virginia, they didn’t necessarily shut down Loyola’s offense. The Greyhounds shot 44% from three and 39% overall. Plus, they hit a perfect 8-of-8 from the line. If it weren’t for their 18 turnovers, you could say Loyola played a solid game. But that speaks to just how good Virginia really is. Putting up 61 points isn’t a lack of offense on Loyola’s part. But Virginia’s defense, specifically their 14 steals, limited Greyhound possessions. And of course, the ’Hoos were efficient on their own end of the court, leaving the Greyhounds in the dust. Virginia’s playing unselfish ball — and the bench contributed Virginia’s continued to build on their unselfish play. I’d credit it to good coaching as much as I would a returning roster. There’s an undeniable chemistry on the floor. They just didn’t miss a beat. Virginia displayed textbook ball movement. Four of their five starters scored double digits, and the bench contributed 40 points to the win, including Martin Carrere and Jan Vide with eight apiece. That balance matters when a starter like Johann Grünloh comes into the night 1-of-14 from three. He finally landed one on Friday, but the team’s overall performance can make up for a starter’s slump. But it’s not just on offense. Virginia’s man-to-man defense is so effective because of their solid help. The help isn’t half-baked. The bigs are quickly sliding into the double team on the block long enough to disrupt the offense; the help on the drive isn’t exposing the lane or leaving the weak side vulnerable; there’s no hesitation defending the pick. In the second half, Thijs De Ridder had a messy close-out, but the help behind him held up, and the possession ended in — you guessed it — a shot-clock

item.title: Infantino hails Warri Stadium, wants football in every community
item.description: FIFA President Gianni Infantino has praised the renovated Warri City Stadium in Delta State, saying football development must extend beyond major stadiums to local communities. Infantino spoke during a visit to Warri, where he attended the commissioning of the renovated stadium and upgraded sporting facilities. The FIFA president said football should be accessible to everyone, regardless of their location, adding that smaller stadiums play an important role in bringing the sport closer to communities. “Yeah, that’s what football is about, isn’t it? It’s for everyone, everywhere,” Infantino told reporters in Warri yesterday. “It’s big stadiums, it’s the World Cup, but it’s also smaller stadiums. It’s the proximity, and to be here in Warri for me is a fantastic occasion to showcase what we are about in FIFA, what we are about in football.” Infantino also expressed appreciation for the warm reception he received in Nigeria and across Africa, attributing the relationship to years of collaboration and football development projects aimed at improving the lives of young people. “Oh yes, I’m feeling so much the love of Africa, the love of Nigeria. This is based, of course, on many years of joint life together, of projects that we’ve put in place, of changing lives of girls and boys,” he said. Vanguard News The post Infantino hails Warri Stadium, wants football in every community appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Corning advances to state volleyball final; Candor falls just short
item.description: Corning bounced back from a loss in its opener to win its final two matches Friday, Nov. 20, securing a berth in the New York State Public High School Athletic Association Class AAA girls volleyball championship match at Harding Mazzotti Arena in Glens Falls. The Section 4 champion Hawks (17-0) will face Section 2's Shenendehowa for the title at 6:30 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 21. Live coverage will be available on NFHS Network , a pay service. Shenendehowa ended up with a 3-0 record in Friday's pool-play semifinals, followed by Corning at 2-1, Section 5's Rochester Mercy at 1-2, and Section 11's Bay Shore at 0-3. Shenendehowa topped Corning, 25-21, 25-21, to begin pool play. The Hawks responded with a 26-24, 25-19 victory over Bay Shore. Corning then clinched its spot in the final with a 25-21, 25-20 victory over Mercy. Corning is seeking its first state title in volleyball. Corning West won the Class B state championship in 1997, when there were only four classes instead of the current six. Corning East and Corning West combined all athletic teams in 2010. More: Corning gets shot at three-time defending state champions Candor lost out on state final on tiebreaker Candor, the only other Section 4 team to make it to the state semifinals, matched Corning's 2-1 pool-play record Friday but lost out on a spot in the Class D championship match on a tiebreaker. Candor, Section 5's York, and Section 3's Hamilton all finished with 2-1 records. The tiebreaker came down to winning percentage. Hamilton went 5-2, defending state champion York was 5-3, and Candor finished at 4-3. Hamilton beat Candor, 26-24, 25-19, in the opening match. Candor followed with a 21-25, 25-23, 15-11 victory over York, and a 25-15, 25-18 win over Section 2's Duanesburg. Hamilton and York play for the title at 4 p.m. Saturday. Follow Andrew Legare on X: @SGAndrewLegare . You can also reach him at alegare@gannett.com . item.title: ‘Life is Too Short,’ ‘I Wish Him Nothing But the Best’ — Stephen A. Smith Addresses LeBron James Feud in Exchange With Skip Bayless
item.description: ‘Life is Too Short,’ ‘I Wish Him Nothing But the Best’ — Stephen A. Smith Addresses LeBron James Feud in Exchange With Skip Bayless Skip Bayless asked Stephen A. Smith on Friday’s episode of ESPN’s “First Take” whether he had mended his relationship with Philadelphia 76ers star LeBron James. Smith said he had not, making clear that the two had not formally reconciled. The question brought their public feud back into focus, nearly two years after the four-time NBA MVP confronted Smith courtside over his criticism of his son, Bronny James. Stephen A. Smith Explains Where He Stands With LeBron James After Their Feud Smith addressed Bayless’ question directly before explaining why he sees little reason to hold on to the disagreement. “I’m 59 years old, bro. Life is too short. I ain’t got time to be enemies with nobody,” Smith said. “I got a job to do. I wish him nothing but the best.” The disagreement began with Smith’s criticism of James’ involvement in his son’s development with the Los Angeles Lakers. On Jan. 29, 2025, Smith questioned why the veteran superstar was pushing for Bronny to remain in the NBA rather than spend more time developing in the G League. The Lakers’ 2024 second-rounder had just gone scoreless on 0-for-5 shooting in a loss to the 76ers. Smith’s comments eventually led to a courtside confrontation during the Lakers’ game against the New York Knicks on March 6. James approached Smith and told him to stop talking about his son. The sports media personality talked about the encounter in his show the following morning, acknowledging that the 22-time All-Star had confronted him as a father protecting his child. “That wasn’t a basketball player confronting me. That was a parent. That was a father,” Smith said. James later explained his side on “The Pat McAfee Show” on March 26. He said he had no issue with analysts criticizing players’ performances but objected when the discussion became personal. “Never would I ever not allow people to talk about the sport, criticize players about what they do on the court,” James said . “But when you take it, and you get personal with it, it’s my job to not only protect my damn household but protect the players.” Smith revisited the confrontation in April 2026 during an appearance on Logan Paul’s “Impaulsive” podcast. He described James’ approach as “very disrespectful” and said he felt James had wrongly assumed his criticism of Bronny was intended to get at him. SEE ALSO: ‘All-Time Melodramatic Flopper’ – Skip Bayless Rips LeBron James After 76ers Star’s Viral Airball The ESPN star has since said he no longer holds a grudge against James.On Friday, he reiterated that he does not hate James and wants to cover the final stretch of his NBA career without carrying the dispute forward. He also expressed hope that the 41-year-old forward would win a championship with Philadelphia. James and the 76ers entered Friday at 13-3, tied for the best record in the NBA. This article originally appeared on Pro Foo

item.title: Even Benny the Bull can’t stop playing GTA 6 during player introductions
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Even Benny the Bull can’t stop playing GTA 6 during player introductions appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Chicago Bulls played the Washington Wizards on Friday. But that pales in comparison to the monumental release of Grand Theft Auto 6 on Thursday. The enormously popular video game franchise dominated the popular culture landscape. Virtually anyone and anything wanted to get their hands on it. That also included Benny the Bull. The beloved Chicago mascot was seen playing the game during the player introductions, per Bulls on CHSN. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Benny the Bull was playing GTA VI on the court as the Bulls starters were getting introduced 😅 (via @CHSN_Bulls ) pic.twitter.com/8aA5cQLgRp — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) November 21, 2026 Since 1997, Grand Theft Auto has been all the rage in the gaming world. Its combination of graphics, violent imagery, and competitive nature has drawn both praise and criticism from those in and out of the gaming world. It is praised for its realism and characters, but criticized for its representation of gun violence and prostitution. Already, Grand Theft Auto 6 has sold over 32 million units and has generated $3.79 billion in retail sales. The sports world is a notorious breeding ground for gaming, where players and coaches get their hands on games to build teams and share a cultural experience. For others, it could provide a distraction. Denver Broncos head coach Sean Payton expressed that concern following the game’s release. Meanwhile, it is unknown if any Chicago players have declared their allegiance to GTA 6, but it wouldn’t be surprising if they did. As far as distractions go, they can’t afford any. They are trying to bounce back from an eight-game losing streak and put together a few wins here and there. Also, with Caleb Wilson out with a broken hand , the Bulls need to stay together and get through those four to six weeks. item.title: Wisconsin guard Jack Janicki suffers foot injury that 'doesn't look good'
item.description: Wisconsin men’s basketball’s humbling 70-53 loss to Murray State was not the only bad news for the Badgers in the Bahamas. Wisconsin guard Jack Janicki suffered a foot injury that “doesn’t look good,” head coach Greg Gard said on a Zoom call with reporters after the loss. “We don’t know specifics yet,” Gard said. “He’s on his way to the hospital.” Janicki suffered his foot injury in the second half of the loss to Murray State. He was helped to the locker room after substantial time with the training staff on the court. He had six points on 2-of-5 shooting before the injury. Janicki also missed the last nine games of the 2025-26 season with a wrist injury. He had hoped to return during the postseason , but the Badgers’ first-round exit did not give a long enough runway for a return. His latest injury leaves the Badgers without a key defensive player and veteran presence as they try to bounce back from humbling losses to Seton Hall and Murray State in the Baha Mar Championship. “I assume we’ll be down one for the foreseeable future in Janicki, but we’ve got to have upperclassmen that have been through the fire here at Wisconsin step up and help some of these new guys.” This article originally appeared on Milwaukee Journal Sentinel: Wisconsin guard Jack Janicki suffers foot injury that 'doesn't look good'

item.title: Lagos renews campaign against open defecation
item.description: …Calls for improved sanitation, gender-sensitive toilet facilities By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos State Government has renewed its campaign for improved sanitation, proper hygiene practices and access to safe toilet facilities as part of efforts to eliminate open defecation and promote public health. The Special Adviser to the Governor on Environment, Olakunle Akodu, and the Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services, Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources, Tajudeen Gaji, made the call on Friday as the state joined the rest of the world to commemorate World Toilet Day at Alausa, Ikeja. The 2026 celebration was held under the theme, “Sanitation and Gender Equality.” Akodu said women and girls required toilet facilities that guaranteed adequate privacy, reliable water supply, handwashing stations and hygienic conditions. He noted that Lagos’ growing population, rapid urbanisation and expanding commercial activities had placed enormous pressure on existing sanitation infrastructure. According to him, addressing the challenges requires deliberate public policies, sustained capital investment, institutional discipline and collective civic responsibility. He said the state government recognised that a clean, resilient and sustainable environment must guarantee every resident access to safe, dignified and functional sanitation facilities. Earlier, Gaji, who was represented by the Director of Sanitation Services, Hassan Sanuth, said the commemoration underscored the importance of proper sanitation in preventing diseases, protecting public health and promoting a cleaner environment. He described access to safe toilets as more than a basic necessity, saying it was fundamental to human dignity and public health. Gaji said sanitation was closely linked to personal security, social equality and the fundamental right of every citizen to live in a healthy environment. He warned that inadequate access to safe and private toilet facilities could undermine people’s health, security, dignity, education and participation in economic and social activities. The permanent secretary therefore called for inclusive policies and investments that would address the sanitation needs of women, girls, persons with disabilities and other vulnerable groups. The post Lagos renews campaign against open defecation appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Waste crisis: LAWMA acting MD unveils 60-day action plan
item.description: …Warns staff against laxity, promises operational overhaul By Olasunkanmi Akoni The newly appointed Acting Managing Director of the Lagos Waste Management Authority (LAWMA), Olajuwon Akinyemi, has unveiled a 60-day emergency action plan to tackle waste management challenges across Lagos State, warning staff against indiscipline and poor performance. Akinyemi, who has assumed office amid growing concerns over waste accumulation across the metropolis, said the plan was aimed at clearing waste backlogs, strengthening regulatory enforcement and restoring the agency’s operational efficiency. He disclosed this on Friday while addressing management and staff at a workers’ forum held at LAWMA’s headquarters in Ijora-Olopa, Lagos. Accompanied by the Acting Executive Director, Operations, Dr. Olorunwa Tijani, and the Executive Director, Finance, Kunle Adebiyi, the acting managing director called for renewed commitment, discipline and professionalism among workers. He said repositioning the agency would require active participation and dedication from personnel at all levels. “We are bringing in resilience and a new paradigm shift. It is a new wave in handling waste in Lagos. “We already have the template to transform LAWMA positively. All we need to do is recreate, modernise and do better than in the past,” Akinyemi said. Outlining the 60-day action plan, he said personnel would be redeployed across the state’s three operational districts based on their familiarity with the respective areas to strengthen field monitoring and improve response times. He also announced plans to establish decentralised operational hubs to improve supervision, facilitate faster interventions and address waste disposal blackspots across the state. On indiscriminate waste disposal, Akinyemi said the agency would intensify public enlightenment on waste sorting at source and responsible disposal practices. He said traditional rulers, Community Development Association (CDA) leaders, market associations and artisans would be mobilised to promote compliance with proper waste management practices. The acting managing director also called for stronger collaboration with Private Sector Participation (PSP) operators and urged residents to comply with approved waste collection tariffs to sustain service delivery. On staff welfare, Akinyemi assured workers that their well-being remained a priority, disclosing that efforts were underway to procure Compressed Natural Gas (CNG)-powered buses to address transportation challenges. Earlier, Tijani called for urgent action to revitalise LAWMA’s operational framework, saying the agency needed an immediate overhaul to improve field performance. Similarly, Adebiyi said the success of the 60-day plan would depend on prudent financial management, accountability and effective collaboration across the agency’s directorates. item.title: Nefer introduces marketplace to make peer-to-peer currency exchange more secure for Nigerians
item.description: * The new feature allows users to buy and sell currencies with other users on the Nefer platform, with funds held in escrow during transactions. Nefer Remittance , a financial technology company facilitating payments and currency exchange between Nigeria and Canada, has introduced Nefer Marketplace, a new feature that enables users to buy and sell currencies directly with one another within its platform. The launch addresses a familiar challenge for Nigerians who regularly need foreign currencies for international payments, education, business transactions, travel and other financial commitments: finding reliable people to exchange money with. For many users, peer-to-peer currency exchange has traditionally happened through WhatsApp groups, social media communities and personal referrals. While these informal networks may offer access to buyers and sellers, they often lack structured transaction processes, adequate accountability and mechanisms for resolving disputes when transactions go wrong. Nefer Marketplace seeks to provide an alternative by bringing peer-to-peer currency trading into a structured digital environment. Unlike informal arrangements where buyers and sellers transfer funds directly to one another, Nefer Marketplace incorporates an escrow mechanism. Funds are held by Nefer during the transaction, providing an additional layer of protection while the parties complete the exchange in accordance with the platform’s transaction process. This means users do not have to rely solely on personal trust or the promises of an unknown seller when arranging a currency exchange. Making Currency Exchange More Accessible The introduction of Marketplace builds on Nefer’s existing services, which help customers move money between Nigeria and Canada. Through the Nefer app, users can maintain Naira and Canadian dollar wallets, convert Naira to Canadian dollars and make payments for different international needs, including Canadian school fees and vehicle-related transactions. With Marketplace, Nefer is extending this experience by giving users another way to access currency through peer-to-peer trading. For Nigerians who frequently make payments in Canada, including car importers, students, parents and businesses, access to a reliable currency exchange option can make a significant difference to how they manage their international financial commitments. Beyond Informal Currency Trading The growth of digital communities has made it easier for people to find individuals willing to exchange currencies. However, accessibility does not always translate to security. Transactions arranged through informal groups can leave participants exposed to failed transfers, unresponsive counterparties and difficulties establishing accountability. By introducing an escrow-supported marketplace within its app, Nefer is bringing greater structure to a process that has largely operated through informal networks. item.title: Nwobodo urges ESUT to prioritise innovation, research, good governance
item.description: By Alumona Ukwueze ENUGU—-Former Governor of old Anambra State and former Minister of Sports, Chief (Dr.) Jim Ifeanyichukwu Nwobodo, has urged the Enugu State University of Science and Technology (ESUT) to prioritise research, technological innovation, entrepreneurship and good governance to enhance its contribution to national development. Nwobodo made the call while delivering the 3rd Distinguished Personality Lecture of ESUT during the university’s Special Convocation Ceremony at its permanent site at Ebe-ano City, Enugu State. The lecture was titled, “From Vision to Legacy: Technology, Education, Leadership, Good Governance and the Responsibility of a New Generation.” Nwobodo, who founded the Anambra State University of Science and Technology (ASUTECH) in 1980, said the establishment of the institution was a deliberate investment in the future, driven by the conviction that education, scientific knowledge, technological competence and visionary leadership were essential to societal progress. He expressed satisfaction with the growth of the university, noting that the institution’s continued development more than four decades after its establishment demonstrated the enduring value of its founding vision. According to him, the true measure of leadership goes beyond achievements recorded while in office to include the institutions established and the opportunities created for future generations. Reflecting on his experience in public service, Nwobodo said governments and political office holders might come and go, but institutions founded on sound principles and sustained through responsible governance could endure for generations. He stressed that visionary leadership required the courage to make difficult decisions and undertake initiatives whose benefits might extend beyond one’s tenure in public office. On the future of ESUT, the former governor called for its transformation into a leading centre for research, innovation, entrepreneurship, technological development and practical solutions to societal challenges. He said the university’s success should not be measured solely by student enrolment and graduation figures but also by the quality of its research, technological discoveries, entrepreneurial achievements and contributions to national development. Nwobodo advocated increased investment in applied research, urging engineering students to develop solutions to energy and infrastructure challenges, agricultural scientists to improve food production, medical researchers to advance healthcare, and computer scientists to develop applications in artificial intelligence, cybersecurity and digital technology. He also called for stronger collaboration among students of management, law, economics and social sciences and their counterparts in science and engineering to translate research findings into commercially viable enterprises. item.title: Trump FCC declares California isn't allowed to enforce phone service rules
item.description: The Federal Communications Commission ordered California to stop enforcing its Carrier of Last Resort (COLR) rules against AT&T, setting up another battle between the Trump administration and California over the state's right to enforce its own telecom laws and regulations. AT&T's status as a Carrier of Last Resort in California requires it to offer telephone service to any potential customer in its territory. AT&T wants to stop offering basic phone service to new customers and discontinue service for 184,000 residential customers and 15,000 business customers on June 1, 2027. The order released today granted AT&T's request to preempt state rules, following up on the FCC's previous approval of AT&T's petition to discontinue service. AT&T had tried to achieve the same result in court, but a federal judge rejected its request to override California's rules in July. Read full article Comments

The rover uses its navigation cameras to capture post-sunset clouds, called twilight clouds, which appear for only a short time each fall over Gale Crater, which it has been exploring for more than 14 years. Curiosity was built by NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory, which is managed by Caltech in Pasadena, California. item.title: Google rolls out new search homepage with AI chat history and no search button
item.description: Google's flagship search experience is evolving into an AI experience with stunning speed. Even time-tested elements of search are getting AI makeovers, and the latest to get this treatment is the search homepage on Google.com. A redesign that's been in testing for the last few weeks is now official, bringing easier access to AI chats and dropping the dedicated search button entirely. Google search VP Robby Stein confirmed on X that Google is deploying the new desktop search page after a successful test. The page will now have a few more buttons under the search bar, all connected to AI features. There's an image generation button, one for analyzing files, and one for brainstorming with Gemini. The "I'm Feeling Lucky" button remains, but the Google Search button that used to sit next to it is gone. The search button has obviously been a part of Google's search page forever. However, it wasn't in a very convenient location in the modern interface. When you begin typing a query, the autocomplete suggestions cover that button. You have to click out of the text field to access the button, which is an extra step compared to simply mashing the Enter key to run your search. Read full article Comments

item.title: Meta reconsiders 2030 net-zero goal amid record emissions from AI data centers
item.description: Meta’s executives are rethinking the company’s original goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2030. That revelation in Meta’s latest sustainability report comes as the company reported a record percentage increase in greenhouse gas emissions that exceeds any other Big Tech competitor racing to build new AI data centers. The company’s 2026 sustainability report claims that “our long-term ambitions haven’t changed, but our operating environment has,” according to an introduction from Rachel Peterson, vice president of data centers at Meta, and Blair Swedeen, global head of net zero and sustainability at Meta. In the November 19, 2026, report, they attributed the changing conditions and the need for a rethink to how “demand for AI infrastructure has grown faster than almost anyone projected.” “We are re-evaluating our timelines, sequencing, and interim milestones—including the 2030 timeframe for our net zero emissions goal and our near-term intensity targets—so our approach reflects current operating realities while keeping progress transparent year over year,” Peterson and Swedeen wrote in the report. item.title: 2027: Sowore faults NELFUND, promises non-repayable grants
item.description: By Dickson Omobola African Action Congress (AAC) presidential candidate Omoyele Sowore, Friday, faulted the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), saying he will abolish the scheme if elected. Sowore promised to introduce N100,000 grants per semester for students, saying the scheme would provide financial support without requiring repayment. He made the promise during a live session on his Facebook page, adding that students should not be burdened with debt while pursuing their education. He said, “The NELFUND that this government has put in place. First, our party is going to abolish NELFUND. We will turn it into grants.” He added that the policy would replace the existing student loan arrangement. He said, “We are going to give N100,000 per semester, which is N20,000 more than what they are getting now. For two semesters, you get N200,000 so that you can focus on your studies.” Sowore argued that Nigeria should avoid introducing a system that could leave graduates struggling with debt, particularly in a country where employment opportunities were limited. Citing his experience in the United States, where he said he spent 20 years, the AAC candidate described student loans as a source of financial hardship for many graduates. He said, “The biggest cause of depression in America is student loans. Where are you going to get the employment to pay back the loans? But the truth is that even the loans they are giving to them now, they are not paying back. So it just makes sense to turn it into grants.” Sowore said a student completing a four-year program would receive a total of N400,000 under the proposed arrangement, assuming two semesters per year. He described the amount as a reasonable investment in young Nigerians who would contribute decades of service to the country. The former presidential candidate also proposed scholarships for students with outstanding academic abilities, saying beneficiaries could be sponsored to study abroad. “Grants for anybody, whether… scholarships for people who show exemplary ability. We give you a scholarship; we send you abroad,” he said. He advocated increased government investment in education, citing China’s support for students studying abroad as an example of how countries could develop their education systems. Sowore blamed the decline in Nigeria’s education sector for several of the country’s challenges, arguing that investment in schools was essential to reducing poverty and developing human capital. He recalled that during his childhood, free education and community efforts to ensure school attendance made education a priority. The activist also cited the University College Hospital, Ibadan, as an example of Nigeria’s former standing in the health sector, saying members of foreign royal families previously travelled to the country for medical treatment. He contrasted this with the present situation, where many Nigerians struggle to afford medical treatment abroad. Sowore further recalled that Indian and

item.title: What is the Riemann hypothesis and why is its solution so monumental?
item.description: Bernhard Riemann set out a problem mathematicians have been trying solve for more than a century The Granger Collection/Alamy The cadence of prime numbers has a pattern; it isn’t simply chaos. Mathematician Bernhard Riemann suspected this was the case, but he never proved it conclusively, and his mathematical successors have spent more than a century trying to demonstrate that he was right. The Riemann hypothesis may now be proven , and it could reveal the most basic structure of our number system, while also opening the door for a new understanding of the vast world of mathematical functions. Read more Mathematicians and AI in behind-the-scenes battle over what’s true In 1859, Riemann made a casual remark about a mathematical function in his memoir, qualifying a statement about it as “very probably” true. The fact that he never proved it more definitively has held the world of mathematics in suspense ever since, and the “Riemann hypothesis” became the field’s most famous and stubbornly unsolved problem – until now. A new AI-assisted proof by Levent Alpöge at Anthropic may have just ended a whole era of mathematics by confirming Riemann’s hunch from nearly 200 years ago. “This result, if true, will be the culmination of a struggle thousands of mathematicians have attempted in the past,” says Christopher Hughes at the University of York in the UK. The proof of the Reimann hypothesis is also one of the Clay Mathematics Institute ’s Millennium Prize Problems, each of which comes with a $1 million prize for a solution. Advertisement The Riemann hypothesis has loomed so large over mathematicians for decades because it concerns mathematics’ most simple yet hard-to-understand objects: prime numbers . These are numbers that aren’t divisible by any number other than 1 and themselves, and any number can be built by multiplying primes. In this way, primes are the bones of all systems of numbers; everything is built on top of them. But how primes are distributed among all numbers is, on the face of it, unpredictable. This is where Riemann made an intervention. He hypothesised that the way primes are spaced throughout the number line can be inferred from another set of numbers, now tied to a mathematical function called the Riemann zeta function. These numbers are complex – so each is actually a pair of numbers, one called real and one called imaginary – and when they are plugged into the Riemann zeta function, the function spits out zero. Confusingly, these numbers that result in a zero from the function are called “non-trivial zeros”. Riemann discovered that summing over a sequence of these complex numbers allowed him to predict the distribution of primes up to a certain high number. Effectively, he came upon a formula that could make sense of primes’ seemingly random appearances among numbers. item.title: On this day in space! Nov. 20, 1998: Russia launches 1st module of International Space Station as construction begins on the largest human-built structure in orbit
item.description: null On Nov. 20, 1998, the first piece of the International Space Station launched into orbit. The 42,000-pound module is called Zarya, and it's about the size of a tour bus. Zarya launched on board a Russian Proton rocket . Two weeks later, NASA's STS-88 shuttle mission aboard Endeavour brought the Unity module into space. The STS-88 astronauts connected the two modules in orbit. Zarya was built by the Russians, but it was paid for by the United States. NASA contracted a Russian company to build it for half the price of what the American company Lockheed Martin would have charged. These days, Zarya is mainly used for storage and for external fuel tanks. The module also has docking ports for Russian Progress cargo ships and Soyuz spacecraft that carry crews to and from the space station. Today, the I nternational Space Station is about the size of a football field and typically hosts up to seven crewmembers. But back in 1998, it was a pretty tight squeeze. A Russian Proton rocket launches the core Zarya module of the International Space Station (left), which can be seen in orbit (right) during the first mission to the station in 1998. (Image credit: NASA/Roscosmos) Why it mattered As of this writing, the International Space Station is 28 years old, and has seen steady rotating crews of astronauts since the year 2000 (for 26 years and counting). It is a marvel of space engineering, but every engineering marvel begins the same: with the first piece. And that is what the Zarya module is: The foundation of the International Space Station. Zarya, also known as the Functional Cargo Block (or Russian acronym FGB), is the core module of the space station around which every other module was attached. It weighed 42,600 pounds at launch and is just aver 41 feet long and 13.5 feet wide. Inside, it boasts a total habitable volume of 1,650 cubic feet. The Zarya and Unity modules are connecting in orbit to build the International Space Station. NASA The Zarya and Unity modules are connecting in orbit to build the International Space Station. NASA The Zarya and Unity modules are connecting in orbit to build the International Space Station. NASA NASA paid $220 million for Zarya's construction at the Krunichev State Research and Production Space Center in Moscow, with work beginning in 1994 and ending in 1998. The module is a central hub based on the success of Russia's Salyut space station designs , with two solar arrays for power and 16 external tanks to store propellant. While NASA's space shuttle Endeavour was the first to meet Zarya (and attach NASA's core Unity connecting module to it), it wasn't until Russia'z Zvezda service launched in 2000 and docked with Zarya's aft that the fledgling space station was large enough to accomodate its first three-person crew, Expedition 1. item.title: Peter Obi Will Win 2027 Election, What Happened In 2023 Won’t Repeat Itself — Babachir Lawal
item.description: A former Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF) and chieftain of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Babachir Lawal, has reiterated that the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, will win the 2027 general election, insisting that the circumstances surrounding the 2023 presidential poll will not be repeated. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Friday, Lawal predicted that Obi would emerge victorious, expressing the belief that the political dynamics of the next election would be different from those of 2023. ﻿ He also questioned the outcome of the 2023 presidential election, arguing that there should have been a runoff as Obi got the highest number of votes, a development he believes would have changed the political calculations surrounding the contest. “Peter got the majority of votes; he didn’t get the spread. Bola Tinubu got the spread and came second. There should have been a runoff in that election,” he maintained. The former SGF further projected that Obi would win Kogi, Benue and Plateau states, while defeating former Vice President Atiku Abubakar of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) in his home state of Adamawa. “I give it to you that Peter didn’t have more spread. This time, Peter will get the spread in Nigeria. “Atiku will come third in Adamawa State this time around,” he added. On the ADC candidate’s chances in the forthcoming election, Lawal argued that the former vice president would not have sufficient ethnic support to secure the presidency. Comparing the NDC ticket with those of other political parties, he described it as a better option. Lawal also disclosed that the party’s campaign strategy would prioritise town hall meetings, which he considers a more effective means of engaging voters. He said Nigerians would look in the direction of Obi due to his character and competence. “First of all, he is incorruptible. Second, he is detribalised. Third, he is a businessman that understands market forces. And fourth, he is a man who sticks to his words,” the NDC chieftain added. Asked whether the former Anambra State governor made any promises to him, the former SGF said, “No, he doesn’t need to”. The 72-year-old said he would go back to his 4,000 hectares of farmland where he produces cash crops and livestock, and watch Nigeria grow. Asked whether he does not want to partake in Obi’s government if he wins, Babachir said, “I’m 72 years old. I have a 40-year-old son. What is wrong if Peter says, ‘I’m going to make you Minister of Agric,’ and I say Peter, instead, give my son Minister of Agric. Is that wrong? In those days when we were young, that’s how things were done.” The post Peter Obi Will Win 2027 Election, What Happened In 2023 Won’t Repeat Itself — Babachir Lawal appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Bitcoin Price Slips to Lows Not Seen Since 2024, Nasdaq Plunges 5%
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Slips to Lows Not Seen Since 2024, Nasdaq Plunges 5% The bitcoin price slid to near $58,300 on Friday afternoon, down about 6.2% over the past 24 hours, according to Look Into Bitcoin data, as a deepening selloff in chip and artificial intelligence stocks sent the Nasdaq down about 5% and pushed bitcoin just under its summer low. Bitcoin broke below $60,000 late Friday morning, a few hours after this morning’s report had it near $61,500. Over the past 24 hours, the bitcoin price has traded between $57,655 and $62,562, a drop of about $3,880. Bitcoin is down about 25% in November, on pace for its worst month since June 2022. Chip stocks drag Wall Street lower Selling on Wall Street sped up through the afternoon. The Nasdaq Composite fell about 5% in late trading and the S&P 500 dropped about 3.5%. Liquidations and outflows weigh on the bitcoin price Leveraged traders were forced out as the bitcoin price broke support. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) accounted for $541.1 million of Thursday’s withdrawals, its largest one-day outflow on record. Rate worries are adding pressure. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent pushed back Friday on calls for a half-point Federal Reserve hike in December. Traders still saw a more than 98% chance of a quarter-point increase, and some strategists warned that further hikes could deepen the selloff. item.title: Don't turn the moon into the Wild West, scientists warn
item.description:
Tereza is a London-based science and technology journalist, aspiring fiction writer and amateur gymnast. Originally from Prague, the Czech Republic, she spent the first seven years of her career working as a reporter, script-writer and presenter for various TV programmes of the Czech Public Service Television. She later took a career break to pursue further education and added a Master's in Science from the International Space University, France, to her Bachelor's in Journalism and Master's in Cultural Anthropology from Prague's Charles University. She worked as a reporter at the Engineering and Technology magazine, freelanced for a range of publications including Live Science, Space.com, Professional Engineering, Via Satellite and Space News and served as a maternity cover science editor at the European Space Agency.

Researchers are calling for a moratorium on industrial exploitation of the moon, fearing that rapid development could cause irreversible environmental damage and destroy invaluable scientific material. Both China and the U.S. are pushing forward with plans to establish permanent human settlements on the moon by the end of the next decade. Commercial players want to build businesses supporting these future explorers by mining for resources such as water , construction materials, industrial metals and rare earth minerals. However, some scientists argue that a temporary ban on lunar industrialization is necessary to allow regulations to catch up and limit what can be allowed in order to prevent a moon rush from destroying the pristine lunar environment. Two such researchers are Florian Rabitz, a professor of climate and technology governance at Vilnius University in Lithuania, and Xiao-Shan Yap, an assistant professor of Earth-space sustainability at Utrecht University in the Netherlands. In a piece published last month in the journal Global Environmental Politics , the pair call for "robust international regulations" and "broad and inclusive deliberation" to allow the global community to carefully consider the impact of economic activities on the moon. In addition to the threat to the scientifically priceless lunar landscape, the researchers also object to the colonization of the moon by a small number of powerful players — namely China, the U.S. and their respective close allies. "With the moon it's absolutely clear that whoever is doing the big infrastructure work is going to be asserting their position, including by defining their own exclusive territories," Rabitz said in a statement . "That shouldn't be the Wild West." Rabitz pointed out that, although the United Nations' 1967 Outer Space Treaty prevents individual nations from appropriating the moon, Earth's natural satellite and its valuable resources are unlikely to remain truly neutral territory if its exploitation is going to be led by a small number of powerful nations.

item.title: Researcher plants 2m canaries into the AI supply chain. A privacy disaster surfaced.
item.description: Researchers planted 2 million digital tripwires in requests sent through a sprawling network of AI services to find out what happened to sensitive information entrusted to them. What they discovered was an ecosystem that leaked highly sensitive data like a sieve. The exposure was found through an ingenious experiment designed to test if sensitive information can leak through the vast chain of widely used AI services and how that information is exploited when it does. Many of today’s AI apps use services such as OpenRouter or Vercel that act as brokers. These “AI routers,” sometimes also known as “AI gateways,” receive large numbers of prompts sent from AI app end users and route them to an available inference engine based on criteria such as the one charging the lowest price or being best suited for the given task. Instead of using Anthropic, OpenAI, or another big provider, the developer hires an AI router to find the most suitable model. Security breaches, prompt theft, and privacy violations To test for potential leakage, researcher HD Moore assembled a collection of Amazon Web Services access keys, functioning credentials tied to empty AWS accounts, passwords for services such as SSH, and unique URLs, DNS names, and private git repository references. None of the secrets had ever been used before, and he controlled the infrastructure that received any requests using the credentials. He then seeded each secret into exactly one prompt sent to a single provider. In the event any of the secrets were leaked, these “canaries”—so called because they resemble the role of that bird when taken into coal mines—would allow Moore to identify each link in the chain that was responsible.
