item.title: What exactly is a light-day? Here's what Voyager 1's latest milestone means for the interstellar probe
item.description: null After nearly 50 years traveling through space, NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft is approaching a milestone no human-made object has reached before: a distance of one light-day from Earth. This milestone — which Voyager 1 is expected to reach on Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026, at 5:16:07 a.m. EST (1016:07 GMT) — highlights the immense distances Voyager 1 has traveled and the challenges of communicating with spacecraft operating in the outer reaches of the solar system and beyond. Astronomers use a measurement known as a light-day to describe how far light travels in 24 hours. Light moves at approximately 186,000 miles (300,000 kilometers) per second, meaning one light-day is roughly 16 billion miles (about 26 billion kilometers), according to a statement from NASA. Although the term light-day might sound like a measurement of time, it is actually a unit of distance, much like a light-year . Astronomers use light-based measurements because conventional miles and kilometers become increasingly difficult to comprehend when describing the enormous distances between objects in space. For perspective on how far Voyager 1 has travelled, sunlight takes about eight minutes and 20 seconds to reach Earth, meaning our planet is approximately 8.3 light-minutes from the sun. Radio signals traveling between Earth and Mars can take anywhere from three to 22 minutes, depending on the planets' positions in their orbits, according to the statement. By comparison, when Voyager 1 reaches one light-day from Earth , a radio signal sent from the probe will take a full 24 hours to reach mission controllers on Earth, and a command transmitted from Earth will take another 24 hours to reach the spacecraft. A NASA visualization showing Voyager 1 looking back towards the solar system as it approaches one light-day away from Earth. (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech) The communication delay affects how engineers operate spacecraft at such distances. Unlike spacecraft operating closer to Earth, which can receive commands and return data with relatively little delay, communicating with Voyager 1 requires mission controllers to account for the extended signal travel time when planning spacecraft operations, troubleshooting technical issues and evaluating the results of commands sent to the probe. Voyager 1 has been traveling away from Earth since its launch on Sept. 5, 1977 . Now cruising through interstellar space at nearly 38,000 mph (61,000 kph), the spacecraft has spent more than 49 years covering the distance that light can cross in a single day. Even at that speed, Voyager 1 is moving relatively slowly compared with light itself. Its twin, Voyager 2 , which launched in 1977 on a different trajectory, is expected to reach the same one-light-day milestone in November 2035. As Voyager 1 and, eventually, Voyager 2 continue their journeys through interstellar space , their growing distances from Earth offer a measure of both the reach of human exploration and the communication challenges

item.title: MSS Celebrates 20 Years of Industry Leadership, Unveils New Brand Identity and Future Growth Vision
item.description: Nigeria’s leading event technology company, Mobile Screens and Sound Limited ( MSS ), has marked two decades of pioneering innovation, industry transformation and excellence with a landmark gala held on Thursday, October 8, at Harbour Point, Victoria Island, Lagos. The event, themed The Art of Experience, brought together an influential gathering of business leaders, government officials, industry stakeholders, clients, partners and friends of the brand to celebrate a company whose innovations have helped shape the modern events landscape in Nigeria. For 20 years, MSS has remained at the forefront of event technology, delivering the sound, visuals, staging and technical expertise behind some of Nigeria’s most significant corporate, entertainment, government and cultural events. From introducing cutting-edge LED screen technology at a time when it was largely unfamiliar to the market, to becoming one of the country’s most trusted providers of integrated event production solutions, MSS has consistently redefined what is possible in the live experiences industry. The evening showcased the company’s remarkable journey from a bold entrepreneurial venture into an industry leader whose footprint extends across every facet of event technology. Through immersive storytelling, visual displays and experiential installations, guests were taken through the evolution of MSS and the pivotal role it has played in raising industry standards and inspiring the growth of an entire ecosystem of event technology providers. Reflecting on the company’s journey, Founder and Managing Director, Tunbosun Kola-Daisi , said: “Twenty years ago, we entered an industry where the solutions we offered were largely unfamiliar and where belief in the future of event technology was limited. LED screens, which are commonplace today, were then considered a novelty. The early years tested our resilience, and it took nearly five years before we broke even. But we remained steadfast in our vision because we understood the transformative power of technology in creating unforgettable experiences. Today, as we celebrate this milestone, we are proud not only of what we have built, but of the role MSS has played in shaping an industry, creating opportunities and setting new standards for excellence.” A defining moment of the evening was the unveiling of the company’s new logo and refreshed brand identity, signalling a bold new chapter in MSS’ evolution. The rebrand reflects the company’s growth and reinforces its position as a comprehensive provider of event technology solutions spanning sound, lighting, screens, production services, and immersive audience experiences. The unveiling culminated in a spectacular drone display that illuminated the Lagos skyline, symbolising the innovation, ambition and creativity that have defined the MSS journey for two decades. item.title: Here Are Six Simple Ways to Prepare for the New Year
item.description: In less than 50 days, 2026 will be over. In January, a new year and Christmas that seemed like a long time away are now around the corner. Once Christmas is over, everyone begins to prepare for the new year and write down things they hope to achieve in 2027. As there will be people moving on to new adventures, getting married, moving homes and countries, starting a new job, there will be people who arrive in the new year with no fully shaped plan. Essentially, it is not because they are clueless or fail to prepare for new adventures; sometimes you just don’t have plans. You just don’t know what to expect in the coming year. As it is popularly known, “He who fails to prepare, prepares to fail.” That only works in schools where, when you don’t prepare for examinations, you might fail. In life, the logic might not exactly apply. You can prepare and still fail; you might not prepare at all and still win. Yet, it is still important to prepare, just for the sake of it; just because you can and you should. Now, preparation in this context is not a grand master plan. It is not some motivational kit that will prepare you for success in 2027. The preparation here is the simple things that you can do to be ready for a new year. Sometimes, 9-5 workers have no idea what they’ll do at work, but they sure know they have to get ready and prepare for work. Even na just one email dem go send throughout the day, they have to prepare for work. That could be applied here too. What are the simple ways you can prepare for the new year? Clean your house Whether you live alone or still at your parents’, you never know how cleaning and rearranging your house can prepare you for the coming year. Even if you sweep your house daily, rearranging your furniture, moving things around, and changing the general look of your house can build emotional preparation. It also gives your house a different look, unfamiliar to what you’re familiar with. Human beings evolve, and while the phrase “new year, new me” always sounds cliché, it can be true. We are not who we were many years ago. Also, whether you work from home or in an office, give your working environment a little attention. Reconnect with people Adulthood is a full-time job folded into other full-time jobs. We get so caught up in its web and cycle that we forget to check on people important to us. December is the best time to reconnect with people adulthood might have kept you from properly connecting with. Call your friends. Call your family members. Arrange a visit or have a proper conversation with an old friend. Call people for the sake of calling. Review your finances and your year Money is important. The amount of money one has in the bank account at the end of the year can define how big one dreams or expects the coming year to be. item.title: Wunmi Adelusi: Why Are We Still Hiding That We Use AI?
item.description: Not long ago, I finished a piece of writing I was proud of — my thoughts, my argument, my structure. I had used an AI tool to help tighten the grammar and smooth the flow. And then, before sharing it, I went hunting through the text to delete every long dash. Why? Because the em dash has become the internet’s favourite “tell” that AI was involved. I was, quite literally, editing my work to hide a tool I had every right to use. When I caught myself doing it, I had to laugh. And then I had to ask: why the shame? It turns out I am not alone. Across a study spanning 47 countries, 57% of employees admit to concealing how they use AI at work. The reasons are almost entirely about reputation. In one recent survey of 5,000 desk workers, nearly half said they worried about appearing less capable or less competent, and a third feared they would simply look lazy. We are using the tools, and quietly scrubbing the fingerprints. There is even a quiet hypocrisy to it. Another survey says out of 7,200 adults, 46% said they would not disclose AI’s role in their own work while the remaining 54% said other people should. I had assumed this reticence was a particularly African trait. In my own experience, my colleagues in DC and Europe — my manager included — are refreshingly matter-of-fact about it. In one meeting recently, when asked to find a specific document in a shared folder, my manager cheerfully said he’d just let AI search it rather than disturb anyone’s work. Someone joked about his “secret agent,” and we all laughed. It was open, unbothered, upfront. I had concluded that we, of African descent, were simply more conservative, more inclined to glorify the heavy lifting, to wear “I stayed up all night doing it myself” as a badge of honour. But the research corrected me. This isn’t cultural; it’s universal. Employees across the US, UK, Europe, Latin America, Japan and Australia hide their AI use at strikingly similar rates. Even leadership does it. In some studies, managers conceal their AI use more than junior staff do. So perhaps the real question is why do we treat AI-assisted work as less credible than work done the hard way? I’ve even heard of recruiters downgrading CVs that look AI-generated, penalising the polish itself. But surely the more useful question is whether the substance behind it is real. A candidate who used a tool to sharpen how they present genuine experience hasn’t cheated; they’ve shown resourcefulness. The due diligence should be on verifying the claims, not on detecting the dashes. Screening out the tell, rather than testing the truth, risks rejecting capable people for the crime of being efficient. Because when you think about it, the logic is backwards. Using AI well is not a shortcut that replaces thinking; it is a skill that reveals it. You cannot get something excellent out of these tools without putting something substantial in. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. Croix Bethune, left, celebrates scoring a goal with Kansas City Current teammate Lo’eau LaBonta during an NWSL playoff match in New York, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images “I think that’s also part of the sadness,” head coach Juan Carlos Amorós said. “I think we never know what would have happened if we played on a good pitch. I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable.” Tickets for the semifinal were reallotted and grabbed up in a hurry, while Gotham officials ground on the logistics of moving their game-day operations. “Obviously not ideal we had to change stadiums, but … I think that’s really awesome to come into a new environment, a new stadium, you have to adapt, you have to make sure you can bring that energy and our supporters did that tonight and that’s incredible,” Gotham midfielder Savannah McCaskill said. item.title: The Macallan Unveils A Night on Earth: The First Light in Nigeria
item.description: The Macallan , the renowned single malt Scotch whisky, officially launched “A Night on Earth: The First Light in Nigeria” at an exclusive event held at the Radisson Blu, Victoria Island, Lagos. The launch introduced the fourth release in the brand’s limited-edition A Night on Earth series, with retail partners Booze.ng, Drinks.ng, Barrels and Naijaliquor and others supporting its presence in the Nigerian market ahead of the festive season. The launch brought the story behind The First Light to life, introducing guests to an expression inspired by the first sunrise of the New Year in New Zealand, one of the first places in the world to welcome the occasion. The release explores the anticipation of new beginnings and the significance of shared moments, themes that resonate with the festive season as people prepare to reconnect with loved ones, celebrate milestones and look ahead to the year to come. Guiding guests through the experience was Yinka Adepetu , The Macallan Brand Educator and Ambassador, who walked them through the inspiration, design and whisky-making craft behind the release. His presentation offered insight into the details that shape The First Light, from its connection to New Zealand’s New Year traditions to the choices behind its distinctive presentation and flavour profile. The fourth expression in the series carries its story through a three-layer gift box designed by New Zealand-born artist Bonnie Brown. The artwork captures the transition from dusk to dawn, with crimson bonfires, deep blue fireworks and the amber glow of first light. Together, these elements reflect the atmosphere of New Year celebrations and the anticipation that comes with a fresh start, making the presentation an integral part of the release’s identity. The whisky itself reflects The Macallan’s approach to cask selection and maturation. Matured in sherry-seasoned American and European oak casks, alongside casks that previously held bourbon, the expression presents notes of sweet oak, vanilla, caramelised marshmallows and a hint of Manuka honey on the nose. The palate develops with berry compote, rich caramel, vanilla ice cream and stone fruits, followed by a finish of gentle spice and mellow oak. Speaking on the launch, Hammed Adebiyi , Senior Brand Manager, West and Central Africa,Edrington Portfolio, said: “A Night on Earth: The First Light brings together the craftsmanshipthat defines The Macallan and a story that speaks to the significance of new beginnings. Inspired by the first sunrise of the New Year in New Zealand, this release celebrates the moments we share and the traditions we create with the people who matter to us. We are pleased to introduce this latest chapter of the series to Nigeria as the festive season approaches, a time when togetherness, reflection and thoughtful gifting take on particularmeaning.” With its Nigerian debut, A Night on Earth: The First Light extends The Macallan’s exploration of the relationship between whisky-making, ar

item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: Gotham FC’s home semifinal moved to 5K-seat stadium in field quality debacle
item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. Providing our players with a high-quality surface to compete is a responsibility we take very seriously.” The Gotham FC starting eleven line up before the NWSL playoff quarterfinal in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Lev Radin/Shutterstock Gotham is a tenant of Major League Soccer’s Red Bull New York at Sports Illustrated Stadium. The Red Bulls are scheduled to play an exhibition game there Saturday night, exacerbating concerns about the field quality. The state of Sports Illustrated Stadium’s pitch has been a cause for concern over the past two weeks. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. The pitch condition was once again a major sticking point after Gotham’s ugly quarterfinal win against the Seattle Reign. Retiring Reign midfielder Jess Fishlock called the field “atrocious.” Gotham defender Jess Carter was overheard saying the grounds were “so bad” when walking through the tunnel after the match. A week after Jaelin Howell injured her right ankle during a home game, the Gotham midfielder said the field was “pretty sandy” and “a little unstable.” Amorós acknowledged the rough conditions impacted the quality of the game. Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Corey Sipkin for the NY POST “At this level, in this kind of game, as a league, and we should have a better surface,” Amorós said. “Unfortunately, our club and football club did absolutely everything in their power to make sure that was the case. Unfortunately, it wasn’t. But luckily, it looks like nobody got hurt, and the game was what it was.” It’s not immediately clear if the NWSL penalized Gotham for a second consecutive week because of the field. item.title: Astronauts Across Generations Share the Stage
item.description: On Nov. 6, 2026, Purpose Entertainment hosted the Artemis Celebration Gala at NASA's Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex in Merritt Island, Florida. Held on the eve of NASA's MAX POWER event, the gala celebrated the explorers, innovators, and visionaries advancing the next era of human spaceflight. The event honored the successful completion of the agency's Artemis II mission, marking a historic milestone in America's return to deep space exploration. As one of the signature events concluding the nation's 250th anniversary celebration, the gala commemorated the achievements of Artemis II while looking ahead to humanity's return to the lunar surface through the Artemis campaign.

item.title: NYCFC fires head coach Pascal Jansen after second-half collapse
item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. Getty Images The head coaching role will take on an even bigger role going into 2027 as NYCFC prepares for massive changes with the planned move into their new stadium and MLS changing their league calendar to a summer-through-spring format, which is in line with the European football calendar and includes an abbreviated sprint season that will run from February to May. The club views this next year as a “crucial point in franchise history” and the feeling is that NYCFC wants to make sure it has “the right leadership in place,” the source added. NYCFC will begin its search for a new head coach immediately, sporting director Todd Dunivant said in a statement released late Sunday morning. “We would like to thank Pascal for his commitment and contributions to New York City FC and wish him and his family all the best. This decision follows a thorough review of the season and reflects our ambition as an organization,” he said. One of the biggest problems that NYCFC faced this season – especially during its struggles in the second half – had been allowing late goals that would cost the club points, or matches altogether. And the club dealt with a number of injuries during the course of the season, while also playing much of the year without one of its top scorers, Alonso Martinez, as he recovered from a torn ACL he suffered last fall. Jansen had appeared to hint at questions over how the club addressed some of the shortcomings in terms of player recruitment. In his prematch press conference ahead of the win over D.C. United, Jansen called it a “combination of both” when asked about the role of injuries and filling the voids played into missing the postseason. “These are topics that are ongoing conversations from the start of the season,” Jansen said on Thursday. “So the one thing I want to point out is that we always learn, and making sure that we do better going into 27 is one of the things that we have to realize based on t

item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team. Efforts to build a complex in Baltimore for an MLS Next Pro operation have floundered. (Meanwhile, United's owners have launched a pro volleyball team.) item.title: How the final standings look after dramatic MLS Decision Day 📊
item.description: We've got a dramatic day of MLS action on offer today as the 2026 regular season comes to an end. How the final standings look after dramatic MLS Decision Day 📊 With all games in the the respective conferences kicking off at the same time, we should get some epic finishes around the East and West. Here is how it all shaped out. Western Conference Vancouver came into the day having already wrapped up top spot in the conference, but their win in Montréal meant they set single-season club records in both points (64) and wins (19). Meanwhile, coming into the night there were six teams fighting for three remaining playoff spots — those spots fell to Portland (7th), Seattle (8th), and Real Salt Lake (9th), with the latter two facing off in the play-in match. An impressive win from Dallas and a defeat for San Jose means the Texas outfit wrapped up second place in the conference. And finally, the LA Galaxy saw their campaign in bitter fashion, starting the night in control of 7th place, but finishing 11th and out of the playoffs after a defeat in Salt Lake City. Eastern Conference Most notably, Nashville SC set a new MLS regular season points record after dispatching Cincinnati this afternoon. Nashville's 77 points from 23 wins and eight draws sees them eclipse Inter Miami's record of 74 points. In the playoff race, a late win for Columbus in Chicago sent Antoine Griezmann and Orlando City into the play-in match, and the Crew into the top-seven in dramatic fashion. Elsewhere, Inter Miami let a 3-0 lead slip against Charlotte, who came roaring back to snatch a point. Heading into the playoffs, Miami have only won just one of their last three matches.

item.title: August Lunar Eclipse Rises Over Louisiana
item.description: A lunar eclipse is visible over southern Louisiana. The lunar eclipse was visible throughout much of North and South America and part of Europe and Africa between Aug. 27-28. The Full Moon slipped through Earth’s shadow on Aug. 27, continuing into Aug. 28 for some parts of the world, resulting in the lunar eclipse. At maximum eclipse, the Moon takes on a dramatic dark, ruddy or coppery tint along the covered edge. New Orleans is home to NASA’s Michoud Assembly Facility, where stages for NASA’s SLS (Space Launch System) rocket and structures for Orion spacecraft are produced for the Artemis missions.
